text:
sam: quick share — KV cache stress bench results from this morning. ran both replay harness and synthetic load. tl;dr: replay shows ~62% prefix hit-rate after warmup, synthetic shows ~82%. p95 gen latency is ~18% higher under replay because misses + kernel-selection churn.

maria: can you paste the exact command + env you used? want to reproduce locally :eyes:

sam: sure — harness commands i used:
```
# replay harness (real traffic trace)
./bin/replay_harness --trace traces/prefix_1k.json --concurrency 256 --qps 2000 \
  --duration 600 --cache-size=200000 --eviction=LRU --workers=8 --seed=42

# synthetic steady load
./bin/synthetic_load --model gptx-9b --rate 2000 --seqdist zipf:1.2 --cache-population 200000 --duration 600
```
env: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0-3, KERNEL_SELECTOR=auto, BATCHER=adaptive, KV_LOCK=striped-64

kevin: how are you computing hit-rate? per-request or per-token? also what window for "warmup"?

sam: good q. we report both:
- per-request (did any prefix fully hit) = 0.58 under replay
- per-token (token-level hits across sequence) = 0.78 under replay
warmup: we consider warm when per-request hit-rate stabilizes for 60s. in replay that took ~90s (bursty distribution), synthetic warmed in ~8s.

nina: not surprising — synthetic smooths inter-arrival times. replay has temporal locality + bursts -> eviction churn. did you try CLOCK or tinyLFU?

sam: tried CLOCK and a tinyLFU-ish bleed. CLOCK improved steady-state prefix hit by ~+3 percentage points and reduced eviction churn (measured by evict/sec). tinyLFU had slightly better hit but higher CPU overhead.

sam: also tested batching heuristic changes — adaptive-batcher (group by first 16 tokens then fill) raised throughput but p95 on cache-miss paths increased because it triggers kernel-switches more often.

perf-bot: profiling snapshot (abridged):
```
kernel_switch_count: 3421
avg_kernel_latency_on_miss_ms: 12.4
kv_lock_wait_avg_ms: 0.92
evict_thrash_rate: 18.3 evicts/s
cpu_sys_pct: 14.6
```
flamegraphs uploaded -> https://internal-artifacts/fg/1760854321

kevin: any correctness flakiness under concurrency? we should be careful — evictions + concurrent inserts can race.

sam: yep ran a high-concurrency run (512 concurrency) and saw rare duplicate-key inserts with different values (manifested as mismatched KV returns on subsequent gets). repro is deterministic-ish with seed.
repro sketch:
```
# stress mode
./bin/replay_harness --trace traces/prefix_racy.json --concurrency 512 --qps 4000 --duration 300 \
  --cache-size=100000 --eviction=LRU --workers=16 --race-mode=on --seed=1234
```
issue: thread A probes slot -> sees empty -> context switch -> eviction removes slot -> thread B inserts different value -> thread A resumes and inserts stale value into now-occupied slot -> inconsistent map state.

maria: ouch. that implies our insert path isn't atomic w.r.t eviction. can we use singleflight/compare-and-swap on per-slot basis or per-key locks?

sam: proposed fix: implement per-key singleflight on insert_or_get, plus a version tag on slot to detect slot-hijack. simple pseudo:
```
val = cache.get(key)
if val: return val
lock = singleflight.acquire(key)
  recompute get(key)
  if val: release and return
  insert atomically into slot with CAS on slot.version
release
```
this avoids double-inserts and keeps contended paths short.

nina: also worth adding a "race-detector" mode in harness that asserts invariants after each op, plus a fuzzed eviction window to increase repro rate.

kevin: agreed. can we also standardize apples-to-apples perf runs across kernel variants? earlier we saw int8 kernel fallback causing extra memcpy when miss rate crosses ~30%.

sam: yes — plan is to run same trace + same seed + fixed concurrency for all variants. steps:
1) freeze trace (prefixes + timestamps)
2) set deterministic batching (seeded), same BATCHER config
3) run variants: float16, int8-quant, int8-optimized-k1 with KERNEL_SELECTOR forced
4) collect: per-request hit, per-token hit, p50/p95 latency, kernel_switch_count, evict/sec

kevin: i'll take the singleflight patch. can you open a PR with the reproducer + flamegraphs + harness changes (race-detector)?

sam: will do. uploading repro + traces to /mnt/bench/kvcache/1760854321/ and i'll open draft PR linking perf artifacts. next steps listed in PR description.

maria: tiny ask — include a short note in the PR about perf/CPU tradeoffs for tinyLFU vs CLOCK so SRE can estimate cost.

sam: good call. i'll add a cost table (cpu vs hit-rate). :+1:

kevin: ack, thanks. i'll start on the patch tomorrow.

nina: thanks team — this caught the tough concurrency case early. please keep the harness failures flaky->hard-fail until patch lands. :lock:
